questions.question_english:
A Principal decides to implement Zero-Based
Budgeting (ZBB) principles for the school’s
annual science exhibition. What will be the most
likely approach taken under this method?
options_english: Asking the science department to automatically add 10% to last year’s exhibition expenses to account for annual general inflation
Requiring the department to evaluate and justify every projected expense as a new initiative
Automatically approving last year’s budget amount without requiring any fresh detailed project proposal or departmental justification
Funding the exhibition only if the school has zero unspent balance remaining across all other sanctioned operational grants
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is option A. Under Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB), every expense must be justified as if it were new, rather than simply adding a percentage to the previous year's budget. Therefore, the most likely approach would be to require the science department to evaluate and justify every projected expense as a new initiative, which aligns with the principles of ZBB. This method ensures that only necessary expenses are approved, promoting efficient use of resources.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। शून्य-आधारित बजटिंग (ZBB) के तहत, प्रत्येक खर्च को नए के रूप में औचित्य देना आवश्यक है, न कि पिछले वर्ष के बजट में केवल एक प्रतिशत जोड़ना। इसलिए, सबसे संभावित दृष्टिकोण होगा कि विज्ञान विभाग से हर अनुमानित खर्च को एक नए पहल के रूप में मूल्यांकन और औचित्य देने की आवश्यकता हो, जो ZBB के सिद्धांतों के साथ मेल खाता है। यह विधि सुनिश्चित करती है कि केवल आवश्यक खर्चों को मंजूरी दी जाए, जिससे संसाधनों का कुशल उपयोग होता है।
questions.topic: Leave and Leave Travel Concession LTC Rules
key_facts: ZBB requires justification for all expenses as if they were new.
It promotes efficient use of resources by evaluating each expense.
Printed answer key: (A) Asking the science department to automatically add 10% to last year’s exhibition expenses to account for annual general inflation.

questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is option C. Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB) does not rely on the previous year's budget as a baseline; instead, it starts from a 'zero base' and requires justification for all expenses. Incremental Budgeting, on the other hand, uses the previous year's budget as a starting point and only justifies changes or additional amounts. This fundamental difference allows ZBB to allocate resources more efficiently based on current needs rather than historical spending patterns.

questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is option D. The assertion is false because Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB) does not prevent the continuation of obsolete programs; rather, it requires justification for all expenses from scratch. Therefore, while both statements have elements of truth, they do not correlate as the assertion suggests.
